channel.title: Web3 Hub
channel.description: Web3 Hub reports crypto news: Bitcoin and Ethereum, exchanges, DeFi protocols, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and network upgrades.

item.title: Monero Restore Height Can Hide a Bridge Refund
item.description: Monero restore height sets the first block a wallet scans; if it starts too late, a bridge refund may stay hidden until the wallet rescans from earlier.

item.title: Why Bridges Pause During Chain Hard Forks
item.description: Bridges pause around hard forks because validators and relayers need one canonical chain, reliable finality and compatible software before transfers resume.

item.title: Cross-chain swap quote changed? Check the route and minimum
item.description: A cross-chain quote changes when prices, network costs or routes move; check the minimum receive amount, selected route and quote expiry before approving.

item.title: Treasury teams need two-sided records to reconcile Polygon Bridge flows
item.description: Treasury teams should match Polygon PoS transfers across source and destination records, separate pending withdrawals from settled funds and value each leg consistently.

item.title: Polygon Bridge: Check Token Support and Contracts in 2026
item.description: Check the Ethereum root token and Polygon child contract before using Polygon Bridge; a matching name or visible balance alone does not confirm a valid route.

item.title: Five Rules for Omnichain Treasury Governance
item.description: Five controls for shared state, spending authority, settlement checks and recovery can keep a multichain treasury accountable when transfers cross networks.

item.title: How Omnichain Tokens Keep One Supply Across Blockchains
item.description: Omnichain tokens move balances across chains by burning, locking, minting or releasing units; the accounting model determines what counts toward supply.

item.title: Five checks to make cross-chain transfers faster and cheaper
item.description: Compare the amount delivered, every network and bridge fee, route steps, slippage and destination details before signing; the cheapest quote can change.

item.title: Frequent Cross-Chain Swaps: Compare Pools and Relayers
item.description: Frequent cross-chain traders should compare the full route: pool depth, relayer execution, fees, slippage and destination delivery can change the best choice.

item.title: Why a Bridge Route Can Need Multiple Source Transactions
item.description: A cross-chain route may require separate approvals, swaps or deposits on the source chain; knowing which steps need signatures helps you compare routes and costs.

item.title: Compare a BSC token with BNB on price, liquidity and risk
item.description: Compare a BSC token with BNB by measuring its price in both dollars and BNB, then checking liquidity, supply, contract controls and relative performance.

item.title: How to Compare BSC Pair Prices Across Quote Tokens
item.description: BSC pair prices depend on the quote token, pool depth and trade size; compare converted values and executable quotes, not labels alone.

item.title: Poocoin brings BSC charts, wallet tracking and swaps together
item.description: Poocoin combines live BNB Smart Chain token charts, wallet tracking and a built-in swap; learn how builders can check activity and decide what to do next.

item.title: Mantle withdrawals need a proof, a wait and an Ethereum claim
item.description: Mantle withdrawals wait for Ethereum to verify a validity proof, then need a separate claim. Plan for processing time and keep ETH ready for the final gas fee.

item.title: Three Checks Before You Confirm a Bridge Recipient Address
item.description: Check the destination network, address format and recipient control before bridging; a valid-looking address can still route funds somewhere you cannot access.

item.title: How to Reconcile Bridge Transfers in Treasury Books
item.description: Treasury books should treat bridge withdrawals as in-flight assets until destination-chain credit, fees and token mapping match the source transaction.

item.title: Separate transfers and batch bridge calls, explained
item.description: Separate token transfers give control over each asset; batch bridge calls reduce repeated setup, but add contract and failure-handling trade-offs for treasuries.

item.title: Bridge Collateral to Manta Pacific Before Borrowing
item.description: Before borrowing on Manta Pacific, bridge an asset the chosen market accepts, reserve ETH for fees, and verify the token address, loan limit and liquidation terms.

item.title: Pre-witnessing can speed up occasional crypto swaps
item.description: Pre-witnessing can shorten a cross-chain swap by letting liquidity cover a deposit before normal confirmations finish, with availability and fees shaping the trade-off.

item.title: Where Your Crypto Goes During a Cross-Chain Swap
item.description: A cross-chain swap sends an asset through source-chain confirmation, protocol liquidity and a destination-chain transfer; fees, timing and failure paths vary.
